title: Diagonal counit with independent derived localizations
statement: Let X,S be Noetherian schemes and f:X→S flat and proper. Choose independent derived localizations on X,S,P=X×_S X. Let R be a functor on the quasi-coherent derived subcategories equipped with the given comparison to Rf*, and a its specified right adjoint. Let c be the specified right adjoint of the restriction of RDelta*, using a given quasi-coherent preservation witness. Let O be a quasi-coherent object isomorphic to O_S[0]. Then Lpr_1* a(O), defined using [def-pc-derived-pullback-across-universes], has quasi-coherent cohomology; for its corresponding full-subcategory object K there is an isomorphism c(K) ≅ O_X[0] in D(X). Perfection of the diagonal is not assumed. The adjoints are the supplied ones.

proof.text: Use base change of properness and finite type over a Noetherian scheme to obtain Noetherian P. The Noetherian direct-image theorem gives preservation on the standard localizations. Derived pullback preserves quasi-coherent cohomology; the same is true after the explicit localization equivalences, since homology functors commute with them by uniqueness of their factorization through Qh.

The comparison with Qh identifies single objects under the localization equivalences. Uniqueness of right derived functors identifies the transported Rf* and RDelta* with the standard ones. Restrict the equivalences to quasi-coherent full subcategories using the homology comparison. Conjugate adj and adjC by these equivalences and transfer adj along comparison. Apply diagonal_counit_identity in the standard universe at the standard structure single objects. Map hO through a, transport the counit isomorphism back and invert it. The object transported from the standard pullback is exactly the explicit mixed-universe pullback, by its definition.
